questions.stem: A community health clinic is planning a sexual health outreach program. A physician on the planning committee is asked to estimate how much of overall population health outcomes is attributable to clinical health care itself, as opposed to social determinants of health. Which of the following is the best estimate?

explanation.summary: Health care accounts for only about 10-20% of overall health outcomes; social determinants account for the remaining 80-90%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Social determinants of health are the conditions and systems that shape people's opportunities to achieve health. Estimates attribute only 10-20% of overall health outcomes to health care, with social determinants making up the other 80-90%. This is why addressing barriers outside the exam room is central to improving sexual and reproductive health.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clinical care contributes more than this; it is estimated at 10-20% of overall health outcomes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This underestimates the contribution of clinical care, which is estimated at 10-20%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This overestimates the contribution of clinical care; social determinants account for the other 80-90%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clinical care is not the majority contributor; social determinants account for roughly 80-90% of health outcomes.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman comes for a postpartum visit 8 weeks after delivery. She has taken daily oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) throughout pregnancy and wants to continue it. Her pregnancy-related insurance coverage will end next month, and she works an hourly job without paid leave. She remains HIV negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to maintain her HIV prevention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Advise her to take unpaid leave to attend more frequent office visits

choices.label: B
choices.text: Discontinue PrEP now and restart it once new insurance is secured

choices.label: C
choices.text: Document the coverage lapse and reassess PrEP at her annual visit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refer for insurance navigation and a medication assistance program

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch her to condoms alone because PrEP access is now uncertain

explanation.summary: When coverage eligibility changes, continuity of prevention depends on insurance navigation, medication assistance programs and other mechanisms that prevent gaps in medication access.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinical appropriateness does not guarantee access: changes in insurance after pregnancy can interrupt preventive services such as PrEP. To create continuity of prevention, clinicians and health systems can use insurance navigation, medication assistance programs, pharmacy support, referral networks, telehealth, and coordination across services. Connecting her to navigation and assistance programs directly targets the barrier while preserving her chosen prevention strategy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Missing hourly shifts is itself a barrier to care; adding visits and lost income worsens access rather than solving it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stopping PrEP creates exactly the gap in prevention that clinicians should work to prevent when eligibility for coverage changes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Deferring the problem leaves her without medication; continuity requires proactive navigation and mechanisms to prevent gaps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The patient wants to continue PrEP; uncertain coverage is a barrier to address, not a reason to abandon her chosen prevention strategy.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has experienced years of housing instability, food insecurity and workplace discrimination. She now has elevated inflammatory markers, insulin resistance and hypertension. Which of the following mechanisms best explains how her social circumstances became biologically embedded?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune adrenal destruction with prolonged aldosterone loss

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic HPA axis suppression with prolonged cortisol deficiency

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous glucocorticoid use with iatrogenic Cushing syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistent HPA axis activation with prolonged cortisol exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sustained parasympathetic dominance with low catecholamine output

explanation.summary: Adverse social determinants become biologically embedded through persistent HPA axis activation and prolonged cortisol exposure, producing allostatic load.
explanation.whyCorrect: Poverty, housing instability, food insecurity, discrimination and chronic stress persistently activate the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, prolonging cortisol exposure. Over time this produces allostatic load, which is associated with endocrine, cardiovascular, immune and metabolic dysregulation, increased inflammation and epigenetic changes that raise the risk of chronic disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune adrenal destruction is a primary adrenal disease, not the pathway through which chronic social stress is embedded.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adverse social determinants cause persistent activation of the HPA axis, not suppression, with prolonged cortisol exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nothing in the history suggests medication exposure; the cortisol exposure in allostatic load is endogenous and stress-driven.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chronic stress is not characterized by parasympathetic dominance; the lecture describes HPA axis activation and cortisol excess.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A sexual health clinic finds that patients seeking abortion counseling and STI testing often leave before being seen. The medical director wants to address stigma at the structural level rather than the interpersonal level. Which of the following interventions best fits this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Asking clinicians to reassure each patient privately that they are not judged

choices.label: B
choices.text: Auditing confidentiality procedures, scheduling systems and referral pathways

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coaching clinicians to use neutral language when taking a sexual history

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encouraging each physician to introduce themselves warmly at every encounter

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reminding staff to avoid assumptions about the gender of a patient's partners

explanation.summary: Structural-level stigma reduction examines clinic policies, documentation, confidentiality procedures, scheduling systems and referral pathways; interpersonal-level work uses respectful, neutral language and avoids assumptions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Health professionals address stigma at two levels. At the interpersonal level, they use respectful, neutral language and avoid assumptions. At the structural level, they examine whether clinic policies, documentation, confidentiality procedures, scheduling systems and referral pathways make care realistically accessible. Auditing those systems is the structural intervention.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Individual reassurance is an interpersonal act; the structural level examines policies, documentation and pathways.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutral, respectful language is an interpersonal-level strategy used within the individual clinician-patient encounter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A warm introduction is an individual behavior within one encounter; it does not examine clinic policies or systems.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Avoiding assumptions is part of the interpersonal level of responsibility, not a structural change to clinic systems.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man in a town of 900 people has been prescribed HIV PrEP by a telehealth clinician. His insurance covers the medication, he owns a reliable car, and the only local pharmacy stocks it. He has not filled the prescription because the pharmacist is a close friend of his parents. Which of the following rural barriers best explains why he has not started PrEP?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of affordable insurance coverage for PrEP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concern about confidentiality in a small community

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lack of a nearby pharmacy that stocks the medication

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited public transportation to reach a pharmacy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scarcity of clinicians who prescribe the medication

explanation.summary: In rural settings, concerns about confidentiality in small communities can block care even when prescribers, pharmacies, transportation and coverage are all available.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rural patients may face fewer prescribers, longer travel, limited public transportation, fewer pharmacies, limited specialty care and laboratory access, fewer after-hours appointments, and concerns about confidentiality in small communities. Every other barrier has been removed in this stem; his fear that a family friend will learn he is taking PrEP is a confidentiality barrier, and rurality often interacts with stigma in this way.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stem states that his insurance covers the medication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The local pharmacy stocks PrEP; the barrier is who he would encounter there, not supply.
whyWrongByChoice.D: He owns a reliable car, so transportation is not the barrier in this case.
whyWrongByChoice.E: He already has a prescription from a telehealth clinician, so prescriber availability is not limiting him.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman asks about her risk of acquiring HIV from her male partner. He has taken antiretroviral therapy for 6 years, and his records confirm a sustained undetectable HIV viral load. Neither partner has other potential HIV exposures. Which of the following statements is most accurate for her counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He can still transmit HIV sexually unless condoms are used with every act

choices.label: B
choices.text: He does not sexually transmit HIV while his viral load stays undetectable

choices.label: C
choices.text: His risk of sexually transmitting HIV is lowered by about half on therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: His undetectable status protects against vertical but not sexual transmission

choices.label: E
choices.text: His viral load must be undetectable for 10 years before transmission stops

explanation.summary: U = U: individuals who maintain an undetectable viral load on effective ART do not sexually transmit HIV.
explanation.whyCorrect: Effective antiretroviral therapy can suppress HIV viral load to undetectable levels, and individuals who maintain an undetectable viral load do not sexually transmit HIV to their partners. This principle, Undetectable = Untransmittable, is an important part of prevention counseling once sustained suppression is confirmed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: U = U means an undetectable viral load does not transmit sexually; condoms are not required to prevent HIV transmission in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sustained viral suppression does far more than halve risk; people who maintain an undetectable viral load do not sexually transmit HIV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: U = U specifically addresses sexual transmission: undetectable equals untransmittable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No such duration is required; sustained suppression on effective therapy is the requirement.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man who has sex with men was treated for gonorrhea 3 months ago and for syphilis last year. He asks about doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) and it is prescribed. Which of the following is the correct way for him to take it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 100 mg daily continuously for as long as he remains sexually active

choices.label: B
choices.text: 100 mg twice daily for 7 days beginning after each sexual exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single 100 mg dose taken within 24 hours before anticipated sex

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single 200 mg dose as soon as possible, within 72 hours after sex

choices.label: E
choices.text: A single 200 mg dose taken at any time up to 7 days after sex

explanation.summary: Doxy-PEP is one 200 mg dose of doxycycline taken as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after sexual exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The CDC recommends doxy-PEP for certain populations, including gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men and transgender women with a recent history of syphilis, chlamydia or gonorrhea. When prescribed, a single 200 mg dose is taken as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after sexual exposure. This patient's recent gonorrhea and syphilis make him a candidate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Doxy-PEP is not a continuous daily regimen; it is a single dose after an exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This resembles a treatment course, not doxy-PEP, which is a single 200 mg dose after exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxy-PEP is taken after, not before, sexual exposure, and the dose is 200 mg.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The dose should be taken as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure, not up to 7 days.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 26-year-old breastfeeding woman wants HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis but has trouble with daily pills, keeping medications private at home and reaching a pharmacy each month. Her clinician describes an option given as a subcutaneous injection every six months. Which of the following medications is being described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cabotegravir

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Emtricitabine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lenacapavir

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate

explanation.summary: Lenacapavir is long-acting HIV PrEP given by subcutaneous injection every six months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lenacapavir provides HIV PrEP through a subcutaneous injection administered every six months and can be considered during breastfeeding. Its long dosing interval is attractive for patients facing barriers with daily adherence, privacy, medication storage, frequent pharmacy visits, transportation or unstable insurance coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cabotegravir is another long-acting injectable PrEP option, but the twice-yearly subcutaneous agent is lenacapavir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline is used as post-exposure prophylaxis for bacterial STIs, not as HIV PrEP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Emtricitabine is an oral component of daily oral PrEP, not a twice-yearly injection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate is taken orally every day as part of daily oral PrEP.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: At a quality meeting, data show higher rates of preterm delivery among Black patients in the health system than among White patients. A resident proposes that the difference reflects a single inherited biologic risk carried by Black patients. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask what social and structural conditions produced the difference

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attribute the difference mainly to individual patient health choices

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conclude that the gap is explained entirely by differences in insurance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the data aside because racial categories are too imprecise to use

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat race itself as the primary biologic risk factor for preterm birth

explanation.summary: When racial disparities are observed, avoid single-factor explanations and ask what social and structural conditions produced the difference.
explanation.whyCorrect: Structural racism can influence neighborhood resources, economic opportunity, insurance coverage, transportation, the availability and quality of care, exposure to discrimination, trust in health institutions and access to preventive services. Because multiple influences contribute to observed patterns, clinicians should be cautious about attributing disparities to any single factor and should ask what social and structural conditions produced the difference.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Attributing the gap to individual behavior is still a single-factor explanation and ignores structural influences on access and outcomes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insurance is one of many influences of structural racism; attributing the gap to it alone repeats the single-factor error.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disparities should be examined, not dismissed; the right step is to ask what conditions produced them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture cautions against attributing racial disparities to any single factor; structural conditions shape these outcomes.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A medical student preparing to counsel adolescents is asked how the World Health Organization defines sexual health. Which of the following best reflects that definition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consistent use of barrier contraception during all sexual activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Normal sexual function confirmed by physical and laboratory examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ability to reproduce without complications of pregnancy or birth

choices.label: D
choices.text: The absence of sexually transmitted infections and sexual dysfunction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Well-being in relation to sexuality, not merely the absence of disease

explanation.summary: WHO defines sexual health as physical, emotional, mental and social well-being in relation to sexuality, not merely the absence of disease, dysfunction or infirmity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The World Health Organization describes sexual health as a state of physical, emotional, mental and social well-being in relation to sexuality; it is not merely the absence of disease, dysfunction or infirmity. It involves a respectful, evidence-based approach to sexuality and relationships, free from stigma, discrimination, coercion and violence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A single behavior does not define sexual health, which is a state of physical, emotional, mental and social well-being.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The definition is not limited to physical function; it includes emotional, mental and social well-being.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sexual health is not defined by reproductive capacity; it concerns well-being in relation to sexuality.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The WHO definition explicitly states that sexual health is not merely the absence of disease, dysfunction or infirmity.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman seen for vaginal discharge discloses that she sometimes exchanges sex for a place to stay. She appears anxious and asks whether this will be written in her chart. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Advise her to stop exchanging sex for housing before any prevention options are offered

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assess her safety and possible coercion without assumptions, and offer HIV testing and PrEP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Notify law enforcement so that the exchange of sex for housing can be investigated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Postpone HIV prevention counseling until she has found stable housing of her own

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tell her that she lacks autonomy in these exchanges and refer her to a trafficking hotline

explanation.summary: For patients engaged in commercial or survival sex, provide confidential, trauma-informed care: assess safety and coercion without assumptions and offer testing and PrEP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Housing instability, violence, stigma, criminalization and difficulty negotiating protective measures can increase exposure to HIV and STIs, and confidentiality concerns can suppress care-seeking. Clinicians should provide respectful, confidential, trauma-informed care, assess safety and potential coercion without assumptions, and discuss HIV testing and PrEP options, including long-acting formulations, in a way that supports informed choice and autonomy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Care should be voluntary and patient-centered; requiring behavior change before offering prevention is a barrier to care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reporting to police would undermine confidentiality and trust; criminalization is itself a structural factor that raises risk and deters care.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Delaying prevention leaves her exposed; testing and PrEP should be discussed now in a patient-centered way.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clinicians should not assume a patient's circumstances or level of autonomy based solely on disclosure of commercial or survival sex.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman who is 3 months postpartum and exclusively breastfeeding wants to start HIV PrEP because her partner's HIV care was recently interrupted. She has stable insurance, a pharmacy next to her office and says she prefers taking a pill each morning with her vitamins. Her current HIV test is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate PrEP regimen for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daily oral cabotegravir taken until breastfeeding ends

choices.label: B
choices.text: Daily oral emtricitabine monotherapy until weaning is complete

choices.label: C
choices.text: Daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single 200 mg doxycycline dose after each sexual exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Subcutaneous lenacapavir injection given every 6 months

explanation.summary: Daily oral TDF/FTC has been widely studied in pregnancy and breastfeeding and suits a patient who prefers a daily oral strategy; the choice comes from shared decision-making.
explanation.whyCorrect: PrEP options discussed during breastfeeding include daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine, long-acting injectable lenacapavir and long-acting injectable cabotegravir. TDF/FTC has been widely studied in pregnant and breastfeeding populations and suits patients who prefer a daily oral strategy. Because this patient states that preference and has no adherence, storage, pharmacy or coverage barriers, shared decision-making points to daily oral TDF/FTC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cabotegravir is discussed as a long-acting injectable PrEP option, not a daily oral regimen for this purpose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Emtricitabine alone is not a PrEP regimen; the oral option studied in breastfeeding is tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxy-PEP prevents bacterial STIs, not HIV, and is not HIV PrEP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lenacapavir is an option, but she prefers a daily pill and has none of the barriers its long interval is meant to overcome.

questions.topicName: Social Determinants of Sexual and Reproductive Health

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman presents with a wrist sprain. She discloses that the man she dated until last year still follows her to work, tracks her phone, and recently shoved her into a wall. Which form of gender-based violence does her experience represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community violence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Harmful cultural practice

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intimate partner violence

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sex trafficking

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual exploitation

explanation.summary: Intimate partner violence, the most common form of GBV, includes stalking, coercive control, and physical violence by a current or former partner.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intimate partner violence encompasses physical violence, sexual violence, stalking, coercive control, or psychological harm by a current OR former intimate partner. Following her, tracking her phone, and shoving her are stalking, controlling behavior, and physical violence by an ex-partner. IPV is the most common form of gender-based violence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The perpetrator is a former intimate partner, which defines IPV rather than violence from the community.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Harmful cultural practices are practices such as FGM, forced marriage, or virginity testing, not an ex-partner's stalking.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex trafficking involves commercial or other sexual activity obtained by force, fraud, or coercion; no sexual activity is described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual exploitation involves sexual activity where meaningful consent cannot be given; none is described.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man tells his primary care physician during an annual visit that he was sexually assaulted at a party 3 weeks ago. He becomes tearful and stops talking. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acknowledge his experience and offer support

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrange forensic evidence collection at once

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask him to describe the assault in full detail

choices.label: D
choices.text: Begin a genital examination to look for injury

choices.label: E
choices.text: Contact law enforcement to file a police report

explanation.summary: The first step in caring for any person who has experienced violence is to acknowledge their experience and create a supportive environment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states the first step in caring for a patient who has experienced violence is to acknowledge their experience and create a supportive, respectful environment. Gender-based violence can affect people of any gender, so a male survivor is approached the same way.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Forensic collection is offered when indicated and desired by the patient, not imposed as the first step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Patients should share information at their own pace; demanding a full detailed account first is not trauma-informed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Examination requires consent and comes after the patient feels safe; it is not the first step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Medical care is not contingent on law enforcement involvement, and reporting an adult's assault is not the initial response.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is transferred to the emergency department from an urgent care clinic after a sexual assault. The transfer note contains a detailed, well-documented account of the event. The emergency physician is about to take a history. Which of the following approaches is most consistent with recommended practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin by asking whether her husband was the assailant

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have her retell the full event to check its consistency

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review the note and ask open-ended questions at her pace

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start with detailed questions about her sexual history

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use a rapid series of closed yes/no questions to save time

explanation.summary: Survivors should not be made to recount adequately documented events; use open-ended, nonjudgmental questions at the patient's pace.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients should not be asked to repeatedly recount events when the relevant information has already been adequately documented. Recommended practice is to use open-ended, nonjudgmental questions and let the patient share at her own pace, avoiding unnecessary repetition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clinicians should avoid assumptions about relationships, gender, or the circumstances of the assault.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Repeated recounting of already documented events is specifically discouraged and risks re-traumatization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sensitive questions should have their purpose explained and consent obtained, not lead the history.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Open-ended questions, not rapid yes/no questioning, are recommended.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman is undergoing a pelvic examination after reporting a sexual assault. Midway through, she grips the table, becomes tense, and says, "I don't know if I can do this." Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the examining physician?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the chaperone to help hold her still in position

choices.label: B
choices.text: Explain that stopping now will lose key evidence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Finish quickly to shorten her overall period of distress

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give an anxiolytic and then complete the exam

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pause and remind her she may stop or decline any part

explanation.summary: Survivors remain in control of the examination and can pause, stop, or decline any portion of care.
explanation.whyCorrect: If a survivor is not comfortable with a procedure, the clinician should assure her she is in control and can ask to pause, stop, and decline any portion of the care. Consent is obtained before and throughout the examination, especially at sensitive portions, restoring the survivor's sense of control.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Physical restraint violates consent; a chaperone is present per policy, not to hold a patient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pressuring her with evidence concerns is coercive; care and evidence collection are her choice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Continuing despite distress disregards her ongoing consent and risks re-traumatization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medicating to push through the exam overrides her ability to pause or decline.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman presents 8 hours after a sexual assault by an acquaintance. She has a scalp laceration and requests pregnancy prevention and STI testing. After discussion, she declines forensic evidence collection and does not want police involvement. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collect evidence anyway because it is time sensitive

choices.label: B
choices.text: Discharge her with a referral to an outside SANE program

choices.label: C
choices.text: Notify police before beginning any medical treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat her injury and provide emergency contraception

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold treatment until she agrees to evidence collection

explanation.summary: Medical care must not be contingent on whether a patient participates in forensic evidence collection or law enforcement processes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Forensic evidence collection is performed when indicated AND desired by the patient. Medical care should not be contingent on whether the patient chooses to participate in forensic collection or law enforcement processes, so her laceration, pregnancy prevention, and STI evaluation should proceed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Evidence collection proceeds only when desired by the patient; doing it anyway violates her autonomy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: She requested care here; discharging without treating her needs abandons her.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She has declined police involvement, and treatment is not conditional on it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Making care contingent on evidence collection is explicitly contrary to the lecture.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation presents to the emergency department after her partner pushed her against a table during an argument. She has a small bruise on her lower abdomen, says she feels fine, and asks to go home. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Documentation of the bruise and discharge home

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ice to the bruise with bleeding-return precautions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prompt evaluation of both the mother and the fetus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassurance and an outpatient visit in one week

choices.label: E
choices.text: Safety planning alone without further examination

explanation.summary: Physical trauma in pregnancy, including IPV, requires prompt maternal and fetal evaluation even when injuries appear minor.
explanation.whyCorrect: GBV including IPV can cause trauma during pregnancy and increases the risk of placental abruption, preterm labor, fetal distress, low birth weight, and fetal loss. Because even seemingly minor injuries can have significant obstetric consequences, prompt maternal and fetal evaluation is required.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Documentation is appropriate but cannot replace maternal and fetal assessment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Symptomatic care with return precautions underestimates the obstetric risk of seemingly minor trauma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Delaying evaluation a week risks missing abruption or fetal distress.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Safety planning is important but does not substitute for obstetric evaluation after trauma.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl seen at a clinic in Arkansas for pelvic pain discloses that her mother's 30-year-old boyfriend has been having sex with her for several months. She begs the physician not to tell anyone. Which of the following is the physician required to do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Document it and reassess at her next routine visit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep the disclosure confidential as she requested

choices.label: C
choices.text: Refer her to her school counselor for follow-up

choices.label: D
choices.text: Report to the state child abuse hotline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tell her mother and allow the family to decide

explanation.summary: Physicians are mandated reporters in Arkansas and must notify the Child Abuse Hotline of suspected maltreatment of anyone younger than 18.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under Arkansas law physicians are mandated reporters and must notify the Arkansas Child Abuse Hotline for suspected maltreatment of a child (birth to younger than 18), which includes sexual abuse. An adult in a caretaker/authority position having sex with a 15-year-old requires a report; confidentiality is balanced against mandatory-reporting laws that protect vulnerable individuals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Prompt reporting is critical for the child's safety; waiting delays protection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Confidentiality must be balanced against mandatory reporting; suspected child sexual abuse must be reported.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A counselor referral does not fulfill the physician's own mandated-reporting obligation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leaving the decision to the family does not satisfy the legal duty and may leave her unsafe.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl in Arkansas asks her physician for contraception. She has been sexually active with her 17-year-old boyfriend for 6 months. She describes the relationship as voluntary, denies pressure, threats, or gifts in exchange for sex, and feels safe at home and school. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decline contraception until she reaches age of majority

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inform her parents because she is legally a minor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform a genital exam to screen for signs of abuse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Provide contraceptive care; no automatic report is implied

choices.label: E
choices.text: Report to the hotline because she is younger than 18 years

explanation.summary: Minor status does not bar participation in sexual health care, and sexual activity in a minor is not automatic proof of abuse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Key takeaways: minor status does not equal inability to participate in sexual health care, and sexual activity in a minor does not equal automatic proof of abuse. The clinician assesses age, age difference, voluntariness, coercion, capacity, power differential, exploitation, and immediate safety; here none suggests abuse, so she should receive the care she requested.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Minor status does not preclude participation in sexual health care or decisions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Breaching her confidentiality is not required simply because she is a minor seeking sexual health care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An exam looking for abuse is not indicated when her assessment raises no concern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Being younger than 18 and sexually active is not by itself reportable maltreatment; the full set of factors must be assessed.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with facial bruising discloses intimate partner violence. After discussing options, she declines referral to a shelter and chooses to return home with a safety plan she helped design. The physician respects her decision and arranges follow-up. Which ethical principle is most directly upheld?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beneficence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Justice

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nondiscrimination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonmaleficence

explanation.summary: Respecting an informed survivor's own choices about her care and safety upholds autonomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autonomy is one of the four foundational principles of biomedical ethics applied to survivor care. Trauma-informed care seeks to preserve patient autonomy, and the patient's own goals and priorities should guide safety planning; honoring her informed decision to decline a shelter reflects autonomy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beneficence (acting for her benefit) might favor the shelter; it is not the principle honored by deferring to her choice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Justice concerns fair and equitable treatment and resource allocation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nondiscrimination is a guiding principle about equal care across groups, not about honoring her decision.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nonmaleficence concerns avoiding harm, not respecting her decision-making.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 12 weeks' gestation attends her first prenatal visit. On the intake form she notes that she underwent a genital procedure as a child in her country of origin. She appears calm and has no current complaints. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask which terms she prefers and what concerns she has

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume she is traumatized and refer her to counseling

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid the subject so as not to stigmatize her culture

choices.label: D
choices.text: Explain that her community's practice is inherently harmful

choices.label: E
choices.text: Schedule deinfibulation before discussing her goals

explanation.summary: Cultural humility with FGM means asking the patient's preferred terminology, concerns, and goals rather than assuming how she experiences it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinicians should not assume that a patient endorses, rejects, regrets, or identifies as traumatized by FGM. The clinician should ask about the terminology the patient prefers, current symptoms or concerns, prior health experiences, sexual and reproductive goals, pregnancy or childbirth concerns, and her preferences regarding examination or treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Assuming trauma contradicts cultural humility; individual experiences of FGM differ.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Avoiding the topic neglects potential obstetric and gynecologic concerns she may have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clinicians should avoid characterizing entire communities as harmful.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Procedures are planned around the patient's goals and preferences, not before learning them.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is evaluated in the emergency department after reporting a sexual assault. An officer accompanying her asks the physician to document whether her hymen is intact so that investigators can establish her prior sexual history. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An intact hymen excludes a penetrative assault

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hymen appearance separates consensual from forced sex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hymen findings do not reliably reveal sexual history

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hymen inspection is a standard forensic component

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hymenal tears reliably date the last intercourse

explanation.summary: Hymen appearance does not reliably indicate prior sexual activity in postpubertal individuals, and virginity examinations are not recommended.
explanation.whyCorrect: WHO does not recommend inspection of the genitalia to assess virginity. Physical findings, including the appearance or presence of a hymen, do not reliably indicate prior sexual activity in postpubertal individuals, and in sexual assault evaluation such examinations provide no useful evidence about sexual history.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hymen findings are unreliable indicators of sexual activity; an intact hymen does not exclude penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Physical findings of the hymen cannot establish whether sexual activity was consensual.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Such examinations are specifically not recommended as part of the sexual assault assessment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The hymen cannot reliably indicate prior sexual activity, much less date it.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 33-year-old uninsured woman arrives at the emergency department of a hospital covered by EMTALA with facial fractures after an assault. A registration clerk suggests redirecting her to a county clinic because she cannot pay. Under EMTALA, which of the following must the hospital provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A screening exam, then stabilization or transfer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forensic evidence collection before any treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Police notification before examination can begin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transfer to a SANE facility before any screening

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment only once insurance or payment is verified

explanation.summary: EMTALA requires a medical screening examination and, if an emergency condition is found, stabilizing treatment or appropriate transfer.
explanation.whyCorrect: In emergency settings, EMTALA requires covered hospitals to provide an appropriate medical screening examination and, when an emergency medical condition is identified, stabilizing treatment within the hospital's capabilities or an appropriate transfer. Ability to pay does not change this obligation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Forensic collection is optional and patient-directed; it is not an EMTALA prerequisite to care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: EMTALA does not make screening contingent on police notification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transfer before a screening exam bypasses the required medical screening examination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: EMTALA screening and stabilization are not conditioned on payment or insurance.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A county health department opens a clinic offering counseling on contraceptive methods, prenatal monitoring through delivery, evaluation and treatment of infertility, and safe abortion services. Within the commonly accepted elements of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), these services most directly fall under which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive justice

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Reproductive health covers contraception information, pregnancy and childbirth care, infertility treatment, and safe abortion services.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reproductive health is defined as access to information on the reproductive system and contraception, health care related to pregnancy monitoring and childbirth, infertility treatment services, and safe abortion services. Every service offered by this clinic falls within that element.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive justice is a framework about the social and structural conditions that make choice achievable; it is not one of the four SRHR elements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reproductive rights are the rights to privacy, informed consent, and reproductive decisions free of stigma or discrimination, not the services themselves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sexual health covers STI prevention and treatment, reproductive system cancers, and counseling for sexual dysfunction, not prenatal, infertility, or abortion care.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual rights concern access to information about sexuality and the pursuit of a safe and pleasurable sexual life; they are entitlements, not a service list.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man attends a clinic that offers treatment for gonorrhea and syphilis, screening for reproductive system cancers, and counseling for erectile dysfunction. These services best represent which element of sexual and reproductive health and rights?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Sexual health covers STI prevention and treatment, reproductive system cancers, and counseling for sexual dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines sexual health as health care services for prevention and treatment of sexually transmitted infections and reproductive system cancers, plus counseling for sexual dysfunction and related disorders. STI treatment, cancer screening, and erectile dysfunction counseling match that definition exactly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bodily autonomy (bodily integrity and privacy) is a principle underlying SRHR, not the element that describes these clinical services.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive health centers on contraception, pregnancy and childbirth, infertility, and safe abortion services, not STI treatment or sexual dysfunction counseling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reproductive rights are the rights to privacy, informed consent, and nondiscriminatory reproductive decisions, not a set of clinical services.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual rights concern access to information on sexuality and a safe, pleasurable sexual life, not STI or cancer services.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: An obstetrician in a state with a restrictive abortion law cares for a 29-year-old woman at 18 weeks' gestation with ruptured membranes and early signs of infection. The obstetrician is confident that ending the pregnancy is the medically and ethically appropriate course, but hospital attorneys instruct her to wait until the patient's condition clearly meets the statute's exception. She feels unable to do what she believes is right. Which concept best describes her experience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moral distress

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reproductive justice

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reproductive stigma

explanation.summary: Moral distress arises when a clinician knows the ethically appropriate action but external constraints, such as legal restrictions, prevent acting on it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Moral distress occurs when a health professional believes they know the ethically appropriate course of action but feels unable to act because of external constraints, including legal restrictions and institutional policy. The obstetrician is clear about what should happen; the law and hospital counsel prevent it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate in care because it conflicts with one's own moral beliefs; here the physician wants to provide the care.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ethical uncertainty means being genuinely unsure which obligation should prevail; this physician is confident about the right course.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reproductive justice is a framework for how social and structural conditions shape reproductive choice, not a clinician's internal ethical experience.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stigma influences patients' care-seeking and access; it does not describe a clinician blocked from acting on a clear ethical judgment.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A family physician holds a deeply held religious belief against prescribing emergency contraception. A 22-year-old woman requests it 30 hours after unprotected intercourse, and the physician intends to decline. Which of the following actions best meets the professional responsibilities that remain for a conscientious objector?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrange timely access to another clinician who will prescribe it

choices.label: B
choices.text: Counsel her that waiting for her next menses is equally effective

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decline and document the religious reason for refusal in her chart

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decline and let the patient locate another clinic on her own

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prescribe it anyway, since objection is not permitted in primary care

explanation.summary: Conscientious objection does not eliminate professional duties, including patient safety and timely access to care.
explanation.whyCorrect: A conscientious objection occurs when a clinician declines a specific aspect of care that conflicts with deeply held beliefs, but it does not eliminate professional responsibilities. The objector must still consider patient safety, timely access to care, nondiscrimination, and informed consent; ensuring prompt access to a willing prescriber satisfies these duties for a time-sensitive medication.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Giving inaccurate information violates informed consent and the duty to provide accurate information.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Documentation alone does nothing to secure the patient's safety or timely access to care.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leaving the patient to find care alone ignores the duty to preserve timely access for a time-sensitive treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conscientious objection is recognized; the issue is that it carries remaining responsibilities, not that it is forbidden.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: In 2022 the U.S. Supreme Court decided Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization. Which of the following best describes its holding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Established a federal statutory right to abortion nationwide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extended constitutional contraception protection to unmarried individuals

choices.label: C
choices.text: Found no constitutional right to abortion, overturning Roe and Casey

choices.label: D
choices.text: Required every state to permit abortion before fetal viability

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upheld state limits on gender-affirming treatment for minors

explanation.summary: Dobbs (2022) overturned Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey, holding that the Constitution does not confer a right to abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dobbs held that the U.S. Constitution does not itself confer a right to abortion, overturning Roe v. Wade (1973) and Planned Parenthood v. Casey (1992) and returning substantial authority to regulate abortion to elected governments. As a result, availability of some reproductive services now differs substantially by state.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dobbs was a constitutional ruling and created no federal statutory right to abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Extending contraception protection to unmarried individuals was Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dobbs did the opposite, removing a federal constitutional floor and leaving regulation to the states.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upholding state restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors was United States v. Skrmetti (2025).

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman who is undocumented lives in a rural county without public transportation. She wants a contraceptive implant, but the nearest clinic is 90 miles away, she cannot afford the visit, and she fears that seeking care could expose her immigration status. Which framework best explains the gap between her legal right to contraception and her ability to use it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gender norms

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reproductive justice

explanation.summary: Reproductive justice recognizes that social, economic, political, and structural conditions determine whether people can meaningfully exercise reproductive choice.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reproductive justice holds that reproductive health is shaped not only by individual choice but by the conditions that determine whether that choice can be exercised. The lecture lists income, immigration status, geography, and access to health care among the factors that affect access, all of which block this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bodily autonomy is her right to decide, which she already holds; it does not explain why structural conditions prevent her from acting.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conscientious obligation describes a clinician's felt duty to provide or advocate for care, not a patient's structural barriers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ethical uncertainty is a clinician's doubt about which obligation should prevail, not a barrier to patient access.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gender norms are socially constructed role expectations; nothing in the vignette involves them.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A maternal-fetal medicine physician counsels a 34-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation about a serious pregnancy complication. State law and hospital policy both permit either management option, and no colleague or administrator is pressuring the physician. After careful reflection, the physician remains genuinely unsure whether her duty to follow the patient's stated wishes or her duty to prevent a harm she foresees should take precedence. Which concept best describes the physician's situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Institutional constraint

choices.label: E
choices.text: Moral distress

explanation.summary: Ethical uncertainty is genuine doubt about which ethical obligation should prevail, without external constraints blocking action.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ethical uncertainty asks, 'What is the right thing to do?' The clinician is genuinely uncertain which obligation should prevail. Because law and policy permit either course and nothing external is blocking her, this is not moral distress; she simply does not know which duty wins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate because care violates one's moral commitments; she is not refusing any care.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conscientious obligation is a clear sense that conscience requires acting to provide or advocate for care; she lacks that clarity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Institutional constraints are external limits such as hospital policy; the stem states policy permits either option.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Moral distress requires a clinician who knows the right action but is prevented from taking it by external constraints; she neither knows the answer nor faces a barrier.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl at 12 weeks' gestation presents for her first prenatal visit. Compared with a pregnant patient in her early twenties, she is at increased risk for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal aneuploidy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gestational diabetes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placenta previa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Post-term pregnancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Postpartum endometritis

explanation.summary: Adolescent pregnancy carries increased risk of eclampsia, postpartum endometritis, and systemic infections compared with pregnancy in the early twenties.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adolescent pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of certain maternal complications compared with pregnancy in the early twenties, specifically eclampsia, postpartum endometritis, and systemic infections. Postpartum endometritis is the listed complication among the choices.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal aneuploidy is not listed as an increased risk for adolescent patients.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gestational diabetes is not among the complications the lecture lists as increased in adolescent pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Placenta previa is not described as more common in adolescent pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Post-term pregnancy is not identified as a risk of adolescent pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A family physician learns that many patients in her county cannot obtain contraceptive counseling. Believing that her ethical commitments and professional duties require her to provide and advocate for this care, she opens an evening clinic and lobbies her hospital to expand services. Her motivation is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moral distress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Paternalism

explanation.summary: Conscientious obligation is the belief that conscience requires a clinician to provide, facilitate, or advocate for care.
explanation.whyCorrect: A conscientious obligation describes a clinician's belief that she has a moral responsibility to provide, facilitate, or advocate for care because it is consistent with her ethical commitments and professional duties. It shows that conscience can motivate action, not only refusal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate in care, the opposite of what she is doing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ethical uncertainty involves genuine doubt about the right course; she is clear about her duty.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moral distress involves being blocked by external constraints; she is successfully acting on her beliefs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paternalism overrides patients' choices; she is expanding access to care patients are seeking.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy in Tennessee and his parents ask about gender-affirming hormone therapy, which state law restricts for minors. The parents ask what United States v. Skrmetti (2025) decided. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It banned gender-affirming care for minors in every state

choices.label: B
choices.text: It created a federal right to gender-affirming care for adults

choices.label: C
choices.text: It required parental consent but left all treatments legal

choices.label: D
choices.text: It struck down the Tennessee law under the Equal Protection Clause

choices.label: E
choices.text: It upheld a state law, affirming broad state authority over minors' care

explanation.summary: Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's restrictions on certain gender-affirming treatments for minors without banning such care nationwide.
explanation.whyCorrect: United States v. Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's restrictions on certain gender-affirming medical treatments for minors, finding no Equal Protection violation under the arguments presented. It did not ban the care nationwide but affirmed that states have broad authority to regulate such care for minors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The decision explicitly did not ban gender-affirming care nationwide; it addressed one state's law.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No federal law grants a right to gender-affirming care, and Skrmetti concerned minors, not adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The case upheld restrictions on certain treatments; it did not leave all treatments legal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Court found the law did not violate the Equal Protection Clause and upheld it.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 27-year-old transgender woman presents for STI screening. Without asking, the clinician records her as attracted to men, reasoning that this follows from her gender identity. Which principle did the clinician overlook?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender identity disclosure is rarely relevant to clinical care

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender identity is determined by the sex assigned at birth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sexual orientation can be inferred from partner history alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual orientation is independent of a person's gender identity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual orientation is usually fixed by the end of adolescence

explanation.summary: Sexual orientation is independent of gender identity, so neither can be inferred from the other.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture reminds clinicians that an individual's sexual orientation is independent of their gender identity. Disclosures of orientation and identity, when relevant, inform assessment and counseling, so the clinician should ask rather than assume.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture states such disclosures, when relevant, can inform assessment, counseling, and decision-making.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender identity is not determined by sex assigned at birth, and this does not address the orientation error.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inferring orientation from any proxy repeats the clinician's mistake; the patient should be asked.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture makes no claim about orientation being fixed by adolescence, and timing is not the clinician's error.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: The constitutional basis for providing contraception to an unmarried 19-year-old patient traces to a Supreme Court decision that extended protections previously recognized only for married couples. Which decision is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eisenstadt v. Baird

choices.label: B
choices.text: Griswold v. Connecticut

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obergefell v. Hodges

choices.label: D
choices.text: Planned Parenthood v. Casey

choices.label: E
choices.text: Roe v. Wade

explanation.summary: Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972) extended constitutional protection for contraception access to unmarried individuals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Griswold v. Connecticut (1965) protected married couples' use of contraception under marital privacy. Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972) extended that protection to unmarried individuals, broadening privacy protections beyond marriage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Griswold (1965) protected contraception use by married couples only; it is the precedent Eisenstadt extended.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Obergefell (2015) recognized the right of same-sex couples to marry, not contraception access.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Casey (1992) concerned abortion and was overturned by Dobbs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Roe v. Wade (1973) concerned abortion and was overturned by Dobbs.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights
